Rows decision/aria-state-lower-case-closed-values and decision/aria-states-on-every-element rest on it; guard `accessibility_states` must stay green after these reads move into escher's helper.

body: The restructure's invariant: the units moved — the driver's command module (its commands as the CLI, MCP, schema and session surfaces serve them), escher's additions to the accessibility node build (roles, names, ARIA states, hidden and inert content), to the key-or-input handler (Enter and Space activation, Tab and Shift+Tab focus moves, select and range input keys) and to the presentational hints — each does what it did; held by the driver's existing schema, CLI, MCP and session checks and the existing accessibility, keyboard and presentational-hint checks, named per body; a moved body no existing check would catch is a gap the plan states.

The accessibility tree stays built through the document's own method and the document trait: escher's helpers split out of the node build are called from that build and live with it, not in a new entry point.

Accessibility code behind its feature: helpers moved out of the node build stay behind the same accessibility feature gate the build stands behind, and the session library still always enables accessibility.
One read per ARIA attribute: the moved additions keep each ARIA attribute read once, in the one place it is read now, and do not split one attribute's read across the helper and the upstream body.
Role mapping and name precedence stay single-sourced: a moved addition carries its role, name or state rule whole into the helper, never a second copy beside upstream's.
The size measure: no file of the command module's split reads 800 code lines or more, read by the codebase-health audit's own recipe at the chunk's HEAD.

The cognitive measure: each of the three upstream functions reads upstream's own score at 547d7514b (19 · 46 · 167) by rust-code-analysis-cli; the one call left in each body adds no nesting or branch to the scoring.

Upstream's text in the three functions stays upstream's: only escher's additions move, told apart by a diff against upstream's text at 547d7514b, not by blame; an addition that cannot leave without changing upstream's lines beyond one call is a fork (technical to the operator, founder's to founder-forks.md).

The session library's public API is unchanged: every path a caller names, re-exports included, resolves as before and no item changes visibility outside the crate; tests and consumers reach the moved commands by the same paths.
No new log site or span: the driver's command spans and the escher log lines keep their names, fields and targets through the split, under the existing target allowlist and redaction.

No new driver verb, field, carrier, refusal cause or exit: the snapshot, actions answer, screenshot and refusal surfaces the command module serves keep their shapes; the readers of one snapshot model stay readers of that one model.
The stand checks' duplication is re-measured at HEAD by the stand reading recipe and stays under 47 / 550.

Existing accessibility assertions are Rust tests over the AccessKit tree run in the accessibility test leg; the checks the plan names for a moved accessibility body are those tests, re-run unchanged once the operator gives a quiet window.
Run constraint: reading, research and the plan run with no cargo build; the readings (size, cognitive, duplication) need no build; the phase stops at the baselines and tells the operator.
Accessibility tier, reach and capability statement decisions: the chunk claims no capability and changes no reach.
Platform adapter rows (accesskit_xplat as adapter, no adapter on stand binaries, assistive technology reach, adapter creation order): the chunk adds and moves no adapter.
Contrast measurement and its thresholds, the lint's contrast finding, stand accent colour and scrollbar thumb stroke: the chunk changes no colour reading, lint or paint.
Open select list paint (engine colour constants, one row height, no motion, chosen-row colour pair): the chunk moves no painting code.
Viewport scheme, zoom and hidpi reshaping decisions: the chunk touches no viewport or text shaping.
Pointer timing rows (double click threshold, double click on the document's clock): the chunk moves no pointer handling.
UI graph state registration contracts (use_graph_state, undeclared, unconfirmed): the chunk touches no app-side state registration.
Cognitive accessibility of the stand (invalid state beyond colour or class, the shared Tab order table): the chunk changes no stand app.
The sections with no recorded intent (SLO invariants and budgets, anti-patterns, decisions log): nothing there to bind.

**2026-10-26-codebase-health** (the dev-host cognitive-complexity reading beside the mutation tier) — landed decision/cognitive-complexity-ceiling's ground: `rust-code-analysis-cli` 0.0.25 on the dev host alone, never in CI, ceiling 15, and on the operator's Q2 answer explicitly no project-wide convention, so 85 functions over it stood untouched. This chunk's three re-measured scores (19 · 46 · 167 against upstream at `547d7514b`) use that tool, and the standing rule its wrap lands as a decision row sits beside that row, the first convention-like rule hung on the ceiling.

**2026-10-16-handler-splits-and-readme** (the range and button arms as private named functions) — the direct precedent for part 2: `handle_click`, `handle_pointerdown` and `handle_key_or_input_event` kept their signatures while escher's range and button arm bodies moved to private functions (`press_range_input_key`, `press_range_input`, `range_track_fraction`, `click_button`), with no behaviour changed, "the parents left above the ceiling at their upstream floor so the next upstream sync's diff stays out of arms escher does not own". Gates, event order, counts and the range-focus block inside `handle_click`'s walk stayed in place. This chunk extends the same pattern to one call per upstream body.

**2026-10-16-file-splits** (five out-of-line test modules; mcp's and schema's child modules) — the precedent for splitting an escher-driver module along its seams with no public item, crate module, test path or behaviour changed. `mcp` got three private children widened to `pub(super)` and no further, `schema` moved its shape types into a private child and re-exported them, and tests went to `#[path]` `cfg(test)` children with their paths unchanged. The crate's private-module count stayed the same. The `command.rs` split should follow this shape (decision/split-test-module-as-child, decision/driver-unit-tests-in-path-children, decision/restricted-crate-internals).

**2026-10-19-test-splits** (eight `#[path]` test children) — moved escher-driver's `cli::tests` and `recording::tests` out whole into `#[path]` children, test paths unchanged, with no module added to the public tree and the scope row unchanged. This is a further precedent for where `command.rs`'s tests go if the split moves them.

**2026-11-14-auto-exploration** (Conventions: ~ decision/unit-tests-at-file-end) — the exception's fixed count of `#[path]` test modules was dropped for an uncounted form. A new test child from this split therefore needs no row amendment.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — introduced the private `command` module beside `refusal` and `schema`, under no `cfg` gate. It holds `validate(call) -> Result<Command, Refusal>`, which receives no `Session` and answers in a fixed order (verb, then the call's arguments as passed, then the verb's arguments in schema order), and `Command`, `Key`, `Call`, `ArgValue`. Trap: `Command`, `Call` and `ArgValue` print an id and typed text under `Debug`, so nothing may field them. The crate root's `Command` is the schema's while `start` takes a `std::process::Command`, which matters for re-export paths after the split.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — set the rule (decision/validated-commands-only) that nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`, and nothing resolved outlives a call. A split of `command.rs` must keep construction of a `Command` reachable only through validation, with no item gaining visibility outside the crate.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (Driver session contract: nine verbs in two levels, the written forms, `command_line`) — `command` gained `SessionCommand` and `validate_session`. A session-level verb is refused `unknown-verb` by `validate` before its arguments are read, and `validate_session` checks the session rows by the same rules. These are re-exported names the split must keep resolving at `escher_driver::…`. The same entry set "one verb table: no second list exists".

**2026-10-12-self-description** — `SessionCommand` gained `Help`: `validate_session` admits it and refuses an argument `malformed`, while `validate` refuses it `unknown-verb`. This is part of the validation behaviour the driver's schema and CLI checks pin and that the split must not move.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** (wire v3, fifteen session errors, the recording module) — the crate-private `call_of` moved into `command.rs` (cited `command.rs:32-60`, was `mcp/result.rs`), so command holds MCP argument reading as well as validation. Citations into `command.rs` exist in the masters and will move with the split.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — `Command::Snapshot { part: Option<u32> }`, with a `part` admitted in `1..=MAX_PART` through `u32::try_from`, any other number `OutOfBound` and a text or flag `WrongKind`. This is validation logic in `command.rs` that contract/validation-order/first-failure and the refusal-fault rows pin.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (fourteen verbs, actions the tenth instance verb; the shared per-verb target check) — `Command` gained `Actions`, validated from `("actions", [])`. The actions read validates each call `call_naming` spells, then the crate-private `check_target`, the one per-verb target check. This is part of what grew the command module; the actions read is a registered contract (contract/actions-verb/acceptance) that the split must keep calling the same validation.

These are the 72 lines that took `command.rs` from 776 to 848 code lines and over the 800 bar (scope CARRY cry-p3m7lb6q). The rows contract/graph-verb/arguments, contract/driver-verbs/press and contract/command-line/verb-flags pin this validation.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** (the coverage reader `handler_coverage`) — the crate re-exports 62 names (was 59), and escher-driver holds nineteen private modules. This is the latest measured baseline of `escher_driver`'s public paths, which part 1 must keep resolving unchanged.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — `run`'s former body became the private `Session::execute`, with the `command` span entered before `validate` and held until `run` returns. That span was built by hand (decision/driver-hand-built-spans) and fields only the eight closed values, never a `Command`, `Call` or `ArgValue`. Moving validation code must not add a span or a log site; the chunk forbids a new span or log site.

It added a trimmed `aria-label` and a bound `<label>` beside the direct text children, and the `Document::accessibility_tree` override. This is a measured instance of escher's share in the file. Rule set: a later attribute read keeps a closed set with no text carried out.

**2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts** (the builder's merged ARIA reads) — the merge took upstream's `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-description`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-disabled` and `aria-level` reads. It dropped upstream's own bool-parsed `aria-selected` and unfiltered `aria-label` reads so each attribute is read once (decision/each-aria-attribute-read-once). This is the scope's premise fct-n7aqpp47.

These are escher additions inside `build_accessibility_node`, pinned by `accessibility_states` and `accessibility_merged_states` (decision/toggle-read-per-role). In the builder: a select option's `label` as a fifth name source, and `aria-selected` read on every element but a select's option. In the keyboard path: a focused select's arrows, Home/End and typeahead through `apply_select_choice`. It also added the `Change` event. **2026-10-31-engine-debts** (a native control's toggled; optgroup; a multiple select's keys; the tree's focus fallback) — `build_accessibility_node` writes `toggled` from `checkbox_input_checked()` under a checkable role and gives an `optgroup` `Role::Group` named by its label. The keyboard path gained `press_multiple_select_key`, and the tree falls back to the window for an unbuilt focus. These are escher additions in two of the three functions, and the 2026-10-31 eight engine changes are pinned by `accessibility_states`, `select_interaction` and `stand_act_select`.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the list's default actions; a single select's `expanded`; `size` on a multiple select) — keyboard additions: Tab runs `choose_current_and_close`, `press_select_key` opens on Enter or a Space with no typed text, and `press_open_list_key` is the open list's closed key match. In the builder, a single select reads no `aria-expanded` and writes `set_expanded(open)`. A multiple select's `size` hints a height through `size_rows`. These are escher additions inside all three functions, and the select-list merge surface is sixteen files.

body: The restructure's invariant: the driver's command module (driver verbs, the one validation gate, the command span, refusals) split into modules, and escher's additions in accessibility node building, key and input event handling and presentational hints moved into escher's own functions, each doing what it did; held by the existing driver schema, CLI, MCP and session checks and the accessibility, keyboard and presentational-hint checks, named per moved body, a body no check would catch moving stated as a gap.

The split keeps one validation path for every carrier: the single command validation gate stays one unit that every verb and carrier still passes, not copied or forked across the new modules, and the fixed order of target refusals stays in that one place.
The split keeps one command span per call: no new module opens a span, adds a span field, or adds a log site; the span stays content-free and a refusal is still logged by its cause name only.

The closed driver verb schema and the closed refusal cause set gain nothing: the split adds no verb, argument kind, answer field, refusal cause, session error, carrier or exit code, and the command schema still reads no clock.

Where a moved driver unit may live and what it may expose: new modules are private to the crate, the public API is kept only by re-export at the same paths, and no item gains visibility outside the crate, so no process-local handle or NodeId gains a new exit.
The driver code after the split still installs no subscriber and reads no environment beyond RUST_LOG; a moved unit adds no env read, print or panic on call-supplied input.

The helper moved out of accessibility node building keeps accessible names, descriptions and stable ids out of logs, sets the stable id as the accessibility author id as before, and keeps the content classes on the adapter crossing; it adds no log site and no panic.

The helper moved out of key and input event handling keeps every key rule it carries (enter and space activation, select and range keys, typeahead kept private, masked password input) acting at the same point of upstream's control flow, reached by one call that adds no branch or nesting to upstream's body.
The helper moved out of presentational hints keeps reading markup attributes by a typed parse, without log or panic, with the select size hint cap as before.

Upstream's own text in the three functions stays upstream's: only escher's additions move, so a later upstream sync meets upstream's body plus one call; an addition interleaved with upstream's control flow that cannot leave by one call is a fork for the operator, or the founder's where only touching upstream's text beyond one call would serve.

The measure the chunk is read by: code lines per file by the audit's own bars recipe (every file of the split under 800), cognitive score per function by rust-code-analysis-cli (the three upstream functions at upstream's 19, 46 and 167), the stand checks' duplication under 47 / 550; these readings are the evidence the gated dependency-and-CI chunk reads, and no fresh audit record and no master row land here.

How tests reach moved units: existing checks keep reaching driver units through the crate's unchanged public paths and engine behaviour through the same entry points; no check is rewritten to follow a moved unit and no new test, fixture, CI job or log line is added.
Every cargo run (build, test, baseline) is held until the operator gives a quiet window; reading, research, the plan and the no-build measurements run first, and the phase stops at the baselines.

The other ten fork-grown upstream functions over the cognitive ceiling stay as they are; the standing rule that a fork addition to an upstream function over the ceiling goes into escher's own function with one call in upstream's body is landed by the wrap as an architecture row, not by this chunk's plan.

Data protection rows: browser history in sqlite, cookies and HTTP cache, TLS, clipboard and file dialogs, kept check files and their owner-only lifecycle, coverage line content; the chunk touches no stored data.

Outbound network rows: outbound HTTP through blitz-net or reqwest, per-host concurrency, sub-resource GETs, abort signals, load waits, CORS, same-origin, CSP, request timeout and response size absences, and the opt-in CDP devtools server; no network path is reached.

Script and resource loading rows: the script fetcher's URL schemes, file URL loading, JS fetch methods, iframe and CSS import nesting limits, stale iframe responses, stylesheet and font-face fetching, SVG href and mask fetches, HTML parsed without scripting, bootstrap native helpers.

Dependency choice and audit rows: cargo-deny audit, advisory ignores, licence gate, engine dependency pins, git dependencies, workspace-inherited versions, skia archive and binaries download, base64, png and serde_json choices; the chunk adds, removes or bumps no dependency.

Secret, token and release rows: CI secrets in GitHub Actions, read-only CI tokens, publish job guards, signing material removal, release publishing from upstream, live-run logins and credential probes; no CI workflow or secret is touched.

Repository scripts and harness rows: cold-agent runs, agent-run, apt-install, the coverage floor checker, the build-directory sweep, and the WPT runner, quarantine and post-results workflow; none of these scripts is edited.
Painting rows: password painted as bullets, select list colours and painting over the page, border radii scaling, inline-box heights, scrollbar fade; no paint code moves.

Embedding and app rows: rdme raw HTML passthrough, Dioxus dangerous_inner_html, Dioxus-native JS evaluation, the Dioxus scheme and form data, external navigation to the system browser, the browser app's JavaScript opt-in.

Engine error rows outside the moved bodies: error pages and their history and favicon skips, history store errors, NetHandler errors, CSSOM script API errors, JS module loading failures, WPT result kinds, parallel style traversal.
Empty or unrecorded areas: the threat model summary's unmeasured items, compliance controls, the security anti-patterns list and the security decisions log, which hold no rows.

File-size bar: no file of the driver command module's split reads 800 code lines or more, measured by the codebase-health audit's own recipe.

The escher_driver public API stays the same: every path a caller names, re-exports included, resolves as before, and no moved item changes visibility outside the crate; the split's modules expose nothing new.

How a test reaches a moved unit: unit tests in inline test modules move with the code they test into the new module files, their test paths kept, with no visibility widened for a test to reach a unit.

Cognitive-complexity ceiling: each of the three upstream functions reads upstream's own score at 547d7514b (19, 46, 167) by rust-code-analysis-cli; the one call added may add no nesting or branch, and the ceiling is read on the host.

Upstream's own text in the three functions stays upstream's; only escher's additions move, into functions of escher's own, so a later upstream sync meets upstream's body plus one call (as the existing one-call precedent for inline boxes already is); where an addition is interleaved with upstream's control flow, it goes to the operator as a technical fork, or to a founder-forks file if only upstream's text beyond one call can free it.

The other ten fork-grown upstream functions over the cognitive ceiling stay as they are, and upstream-authored oversize files and oversize integration-test targets kept whole are no part of the split.
Nothing is added: no new behaviour, driver verb, field, carrier, log site, span, refusal cause or exit code; the command span and the driver's per-call log line stay as they are written.

Re-measure at HEAD with no build: files over 800 and functions over cognitive 15 by the audit's recipe, the three functions by rust-code-analysis-cli, and the stand checks' duplication under 47 / 550 by the stand reading (upstream's duplicated test pairs kept as upstream's); these readings are the evidence the gated run reads for v040-08's clauses, beside the boundary audit record and CI on that HEAD.
Every cargo build, test, clippy or mutation run is held until the operator's quiet window (another project times a mutation tier on the host); the phase stops at the baselines and tells the operator.

The moved code passes the build's gates on that HEAD: clippy over the workspace and over upstream blitz-dom, the minimum supported Rust version, the per-crate coverage floors, and the fast and slow CI legs green as a whole, not per package.

Accessibility checks keep their leg: the checks proving the moved accessibility additions stay in the a11y leg they run in, and stand checks run under the zero-failure budget over their repeat rounds.
A mutation reading of a moved unit, if the plan takes one, is read per unit on the dev host only, with the scoped run filter anchored on the moved unit's verb, and only in the quiet window.
